title: Kreuzberg Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Kreuzberg is really two districts sharing one name.** The old postal codes still split it: **SO36** (Kreuzberg 36) in the east is loud, Turkish, punk and awake late; **Kreuzberg 61** in the west, around Bergmannstraße, is leafy, cobbled and café-slow. Knowing which half you are heading into saves a lot of confusion.

**East Kreuzberg (SO36) is the one on the postcards.** Kottbusser Tor, Oranienstraße, Görlitzer Park and Schlesisches Tor. This is bars, kebab, street noise and nightlife, best from late afternoon into the evening. The U1/U3 runs above the street here, so it is easy to hop between stops.

**West Kreuzberg (Bergmannkiez) is the calm, daytime side.** Bergmannstraße cafés, the Marheineke market hall, and Viktoriapark with the 66 m hill the whole district is named after, complete with a waterfall and a monument on top. Good for a slow morning, brunch, or a family-friendly walk.

**Two food landmarks are worth planning around.** Markthalle Neun on Eisenbahnstraße runs **Street Food Thursday from 17:00 to 22:00**, and the Mehringdamm corner has Curry 36 and Mustafa's Gemüse Kebap, two of Berlin's most-queued snacks.

**Görlitzer Park has a real drug-dealing reputation, and that is not a myth.** In daylight it is a normal busy park; I would not treat it as a place to linger alone at night. As of July 2026 the new fence is built but the gates are being kept open at night after a court ruling, so the situation is still changing.
